niche.diet: Detritivore: winter-killed rosette litter, frozen carcass bits, and basalt grit

chains.trait: Limbless, worm-like body under 5 cm long
links: Slithers through loose basalt scree without snagging legs.
Highlands are steep slopes of unstable basalt and lava fragments.
Island is a stratovolcano; rock is andesite and basalt lava tubes.

skill.effect: Move through scree and packed snow without speed penalty or entanglement.

chains.weakness: Exposed on open rock; vulnerable to beak strikes.
observe: Creature slithers over basalt shards with no legs.
Body presses close to rock to avoid wind lift.
Moves smoothly through loose gravel without sinking.

journal.en: A black thread sewing the scree together.

plausibility.summary: A 3 cm, 2 g limbless crawler matches scree and litter interstices on steep volcanic slopes; low profile reduces wind drag (D17/F19) and avoids entanglement on basalt shards. At this mass, oxygen at 0.34 bar (D10/F5) is not limiting for a slow detritivore.
fixes: A 3 cm, 2 g limbless crawler matches scree and litter interstices on steep volcanic slopes; low profile reduces wind drag (D17/F19) and avoids entanglement on basalt shards. At this mass, oxygen at 0.34 bar (D10/F5) is not limiting for a slow detritivore.

analogues.organism: Alpine collembola and enchytraeid worms in cold litter; oligochaete-style burrowers in rocky soils (mechanism: interstitial crawling, no limbs needed at milligram–gram scale).
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Eats winter-killed rosette litter and frozen carcass bits
links: Rosettes die and freeze when snow falls; carcasses drift to cold slopes and freeze solid.
Snow accumulates above 1,750 m in winter and kills high-altitude vegetation.
Mean sea-level 14 °C, lapse 6.2 K/km; snow above ~1,750 m in winter.

skill.effect: Scrape flesh from frozen bone and rock to extract bone shards and DNA.

chains.weakness: Starvation risk if no frozen carcass found; slow metabolism.
observe: Creature feasting on a frozen bone fragment under snow.
Mouth scraping frozen meat off a basalt rock.
Leaving dark trails on white snow.

journal.en: The mountain's winter pantry: dead leaves and frozen bones.

plausibility.summary: Source carcass bits from winter-killed highland herbivores on slopes and rare upslope scavenging, not giant shore carcasses as the main highland pantry; tie feeding peaks to midday thaw on basalt. Relation to zanco = scavenger of winter kills, not live predation.
fixes: Source carcass bits from winter-killed highland herbivores on slopes and rare upslope scavenging, not giant shore carcasses as the main highland pantry; tie feeding peaks to midday thaw on basalt. Relation to zanco = scavenger of winter kills, not live predation.

analogues.organism: Snow fleas and enchytraeids on winter-killed plant litter; alpine carrion beetles and blowfly larvae on thawing ungulate remains (mechanism: scavenging at thaw margins).

chains.trait: Black, melanin-like pigmentation active during daylight
links: High altitude UV would damage tissue without a shield.
Stellar UV is 1.15x; atmospheric attenuation drops at altitude, reaching 1.4x at 2,000 m.
Surface UV 0.9x at sea level but 1.4x at 2,000 m.

skill.effect: Take no UV damage while active in highlands.

chains.weakness: Black pigment visible to sighted predators; cannot hide in bright snow.
observe: Creature basking in sun without damage, skin black as basalt.
Pigment matches the color of high-altitude melanin crusts.
Active only when sun is up and UV is highest.

journal.en: Black skin drinks the sun and keeps the burns away.

plausibility.summary: 1.4× surface UV at ~2,000 m (F14/D23) strongly selects UV-absorbing pigments in small, poorly shelled epigeal animals; diurnal activity on exposed scree is consistent if pigmentation is the shield. Conspicuousness on snow is a real cost (weakness is honest). Dark cuticle also aids passive warming at altitude, which helps process frozen detritus.
fixes: 1.4× surface UV at ~2,000 m (F14/D23) strongly selects UV-absorbing pigments in small, poorly shelled epigeal animals; diurnal activity on exposed scree is consistent if pigmentation is the shield. Conspicuousness on snow is a real cost (weakness is honest). Dark cuticle also aids passive warming at altitude, which helps process frozen detritus.

analogues.organism: Melanin-rich alpine arthropods and lichen/granule melanins on UV-exposed surfaces (mechanism: UV screening via melanin and related polymers).

links: Wind scatters scent molecules too fast for long-range detection.
Wind force per m/s is 1.6x Earth's, dispersing chemical trails instantly.
Wind force at a given speed 1.58 times Earth's.

skill.effect: The creature sweeps its mouth-tentacles through the breeze to taste the air. This allows you to see where food lies nearby.

chains.weakness: Tentacles are fragile; lost if grabbed by a predator.
observe: Creature probing wind with mouth-tentacles before moving.
Tentacles twitching to catch scent particles directly.
Ignoring distant scents, only reacting to wind-blown contact.

journal.en: Wind lies; only the mouth knows the truth.

plausibility.summary: Reframe as short retractable labial/cephalic palps that probe cracks, under stones, and thawing carcass–rock contacts in the still boundary layer; reserve ‘wind’ for gales on exposed ridges. Drop or shorten effective ‘5 m in wind’ to ~contact range unless you justify elastic palps (then mark highly speculative).

moments: A small black creature crawls over the skull of a giant that drifted ashore, nibbling the last dry sinew while the wind howls across the high slopes.

journal.en: Gusano_Ceniza: Black as basalt, small as a seed, it turns the mountain's winter death into life.
Notes: The creature's mouth-tentacles twitch even in the storm; it tastes the wind for the sour sweet of frozen meat.
